REPAIRED (D020) verify.ps1:35 masked two of its three exit codes. The 'integration-tests' Step block ran three cargo tests separated by `;`, and Step only read $LASTEXITCODE after the block - so the step's ok reflected dag_parallel (the last command) alone. Measured directly: a block containing a failing `cargo fmt` then a passing `doctor` recorded ok=True exit=0. Fixed by splitting it into integration-producer-tests, integration-export-matrix and integration-dag-parallel (one command per block), and by having Step clear $global:LASTEXITCODE on entry - which exposed a SECOND leak that this repair found: a step whose block runs no external command inherited the previous step's verdict.

REPAIRED (D020) verify.json recorded skipped gates as ok:true. link-integration and spout-enumeration wrote { ok = true; skipped = true } when their env vars were unset - the AGENTS.md rule 'missing prerequisite is blocked_external, never passed' violated inside the verification harness itself. Now a Blocked step writes ok:null, status='blocked_external', skipped=true and a reason, and the payload carries counts.blocked_external. The evidence file also lost its UTF-8 BOM (HEAD's verify.json failed strict JSON.parse) and gained gitHash + rustc, so a verdict can be attributed to a tree.

REPAIRED (D023) the step named 'ndi-discovery' overpromised, and its pass was conditional on nothing. It ran `cargo test -p flux-integrations --features ndi ndi::`, which selects exactly 2 tests (runtime_loads_and_initializes, discovery_returns_state_without_crash); crates/integrations/src/ndi.rs contains no other test, and the filter does not reach ndi_io::tests::shim_loads_and_initializes. Both selected tests `return` early when the runtime DLL cannot be dlopened, so on a machine with no NDI the step recorded ok:true for zero assertions. verify.ps1 now probes the same candidate list ndi.rs walks (FLUX_NDI_LIB, NDI 6 Tools, Resolume Arena, bare name on PATH) and writes either Step 'ndi-runtime-loads' or a compile-only step plus Blocked, so the gate can no longer pass by absence. Measuring it also found that '5 live sources' was an environment reading, not a capability: `flux ndi` finds 0 today. Two defects of the same family are still open: crates/integrations/src/lib.rs sets `verified: cfg!(feature = "spout")` (:86) and `cfg!(feature = "link")` (:114), which is presence standing in for proof - the function's own doc comment forbids exactly that.

REPAIRED (D023) `flux ndi-loopback` had never worked and always exited 0. It passed the sender's own name to ndi_shim_recv_create, which forwards it as NDIlib_recv_create_v3's p_ndi_name; NDI advertises `{machine} ({sender})`, so the subscription could not match, the 40 x 150 ms receive loop timed out, the command printed 'no frame received within timeout' and returned Ok. Fixed by resolving the advertised name through discovery first (the way cmd_ndi_recv already did) and by turning every unfulfilled purpose in ndi/ndi-send/ndi-recv into ErrorCode::SdkMissing, which exits 1. An empty discovery list stays exit 0 on purpose - finding nothing is an answer, failing to connect is not.

clippy is neutered: ci.yml:31 runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -A warnings` (-A = allow), so it can only detect a compile failure, never a lint. The plain build already emits ~10 warnings, including dead fields in RuntimeGraph and a never-used flux_app_persistence_load.

REPAIRED (D021) xtask benchmark lied about what it measured. (a) `--profile` was parsed and echoed into the JSON but never used - resolution was hardcoded 1920x1080 and the set was `.take(30)` fragment generators, so `--profile ordinary` and `--profile 4k` did identical work. Now a BENCH_PROFILES table sets resolution, budget and graph, and an unknown profile exits 2 instead of silently benching. (b) Each timed iteration included the preview readback, so the number was render + a 2,073,600 B GPU->CPU copy (earlier notes said ~8 MB; wrong - preview_size() clamps to 960x540). Render and copy are now timed in separate windows, the render window ends in an explicit queue wait, and the gate times an 8-node merging graph rather than one node. (c) With 12 samples, `times[len*95/100]` = index 11 = the single worst sample, so 'p95' was really max. Now 15 warm-up frames are discarded, 120 are timed, and percentiles are nearest-rank with p95/p99 emitted only when n supports them; the per-generator sweep reports median/max explicitly. Consequence for the old headline: 'gen.concentric p95 21.49 ms' was the readback, not the node - on render alone all 30 swept generators are under budget.
